solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Grant promotion and hand in report

parts.note: an advertisement promotes a product, abbreviated to AD

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for hand is taken by its sound

parts.note: a mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A boss approves a staff promotion and asks for a written report to be handed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a verb about giving a promotion; it is the definition, in the sense of conceding a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a point in argument is to concede or acknowledge that it is true.

clue.text: Plant tower for trailer and garden tool boxes close to track

parts.note: an artic, an articulated lorry, tows a trailer

indicators.note: boxing something encloses it

parts.note: a hoe is a garden tool for weeding

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A lorry and garden equipment are packed in near a railway line, with a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' looks like a tall building; it is something that tows. ARTIC is British for an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle-like plant grown for its edible flower heads.

clue.text: Drive to the north in PM being irritable

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Theresa May was the British Prime Minister when this was published

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: DR is the street abbreviation for Drive

explanation.surface: A grumpy Prime Minister heads north on a road trip.
explanation.walkthrough: MARDY is northern English dialect for sulky or bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardy means sulky, moody and easily annoyed, so irritable.

clue.text: Heavy machine to carry over hill

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to cart something is to carry it
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A big vehicle is needed to haul something over a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is a powerful farm vehicle, a heavy piece of machinery.

clue.text: Restraint to consume liquor for period

indicators.note: consuming takes something inside, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a tie is something that holds back or restrains
mescal is a Mexican spirit distilled from agave

explanation.surface: A recovering drinker is told how long they must hold back from drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A timescale is the span of time over which something happens, a period.

clue.text: Desire garment, needing to drop size, primarily

indicators.note: dropping means moving lower in a down entry, so a letter shifts further along

parts.note: a T-shirt is a garment

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone wants a top but must go down a size.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of T-SHIRT moves down two places.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst can mean a strong craving or longing, as in a thirst for knowledge.

clue.text: Gracious person not late

parts.note: a man is a person
late can mean dead, so not late means living

explanation.surface: A kind and courteous individual who is always on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not late' suggests punctual; late here means deceased. 'Gracious' is the exclamation, as in 'Good gracious!'
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, like 'good heavens!'

clue.text: Crack that's damaged ruler

indicators.note: damage breaks something up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A broken wooden ruler with a crack in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter is to break suddenly into pieces, much as something cracks.

clue.text: A federation to arrest revolutionary from Asia Minor

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, an alliance of states

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch or arrest them

explanation.surface: An alliance moves to detain a rebel from Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reads as a rebel noun; it is a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia is the Asian part of Turkey, the region also called Asia Minor.

clue.text: Not the first to tidy and put away

definitions.note: past participle sense: food put away is consumed

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to neaten something is to tidy it

explanation.surface: Someone is told not to be the first to tidy up and store things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' suggests tidying; it means consumed, as food is.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is informal for eating it up.

clue.text: From the East, rogue state causing bother to Trump

definitions.note: an exclamation of annoyance as an American like Trump might say it

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel or rogue
a nation is a state or country

explanation.surface: A hostile foreign country is making trouble for the US president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bother' is the mild British oath, and 'to Trump' marks the answer as American: it is the US folksy equivalent of 'damnation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarnation is an old American euphemism for damnation, used as an exasperated exclamation like 'bother!'

clue.text: After change of heart, endorse tailor

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, and here that letter is swapped for another

parts.note: to adopt a policy or view is to endorse it

explanation.surface: Someone changes their mind and decides to back a tailor after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle O of ADOPT becomes A.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor something is to adjust or modify it to suit a purpose.

clue.text: Mammals decided about following evasive duck

indicators.note: the reversed word comes after the other pieces

parts.note: coy means reluctant to give details, evasive
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the letter O

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: set means fixed or decided

explanation.surface: Animals made up their minds after a wary duck came near.
explanation.definitionFit: Coyotes are wild dogs of North America, so they are mammals.

clue.text: Diamonds buried in eastern settlement by large desert

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large

indicators.note: something buried is put inside, so one letter goes into a word

parts.note: a town is a settlement
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Treasure hidden in an eastern town beside a vast desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' reads as a noun in the scene; it is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone down is to fail or abandon them, which is to desert them.

clue.text: Disapproval from public about HS2?

parts.note: out means known to everyone, made public
C stands for circa, Latin for about
HS2 is a planned British high-speed railway line, an example of a railway, abbreviated RY; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: Public objection to the controversial HS2 rail project.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, but 'Disapproval' alone defines, and the rest builds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a loud public protest, a strong expression of disapproval.

clue.text: Repeated order to wet child — you must release hydrant

indicators.note: putting letters in a new order rearranges them
releasing lets something go, so these letters are dropped from the jumble

parts.note: H on a small yellow sign marks a fire hydrant in Britain

explanation.surface: A parent tells a child to stop playing with the fire hydrant and soaking themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H out of TOWETCHILD and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A twice-told tale is one told over again, repeated.

clue.text: Too much in order to house cleric, retired and sick

indicators.note: housing something means holding it inside

parts.note: OK means all right, in order

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric
ill means sick

explanation.surface: An excessive measure: in order to accommodate a vicar who has stopped working and fallen ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Overkill is excessive action, far more than is needed.

clue.text: Almost agree about where to see aquatic monster's bulk

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters are mixed up
almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Loch Ness, written L. Ness, home of the legendary Scottish monster

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone accepts the size of the Loch Ness monster.
explanation.walkthrough: L NESS is the map form of Loch Ness, the Scottish lake of monster legend; the ARGE in the middle comes from the shortened AGREE turned about.
explanation.definitionFit: Largeness means great size, synonymous with bulk.

clue.text: Familiarity not popular on the street

indicators.note: not means without, so the letters are taken out

parts.note: homeliness means comfortable familiarity, cosiness
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Being well known isn't popular among people living rough.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living on the street has no home to live in.

clue.text: Rough toilet paper, apart from core that's smoother

indicators.note: rough suggests something roughly handled, so the letters are jumbled
apart from means without, and the core of the phrase is its middle three letters

explanation.surface: Complaining that coarse toilet paper, except for the roll, is what makes one smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from core' removes ETP, the middle letters of TOILETPAPER; 'Rough' then rearranges the remaining eight.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilator removes body hair, a device that leaves skin smoother.

clue.text: Test article, two variables, when immersed in alcohol

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: immersed means placed inside a liquid, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: ale is an alcoholic drink
y and z are variables in algebra

explanation.surface: A lab experiment on a substance with two variables, conducted in alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling with Z is the one the wordplay gives.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse something is to examine or test it in detail.

clue.text: Develop plot beside a river flat

parts.note: to plan is to work out or develop a plot
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A developer plans a plot of land next to a river, which happens to be level.
explanation.definitionFit: Planar describes something lying in a single plane, so it is flat.

clue.text: Set up posh kitchen almost entirely for veggies

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: gel means to set, as a jelly does
U is the abbreviation for upper-class, posh

indicators.note: almost entirely means all but the last letter

parts.note: a mess is the dining room and kitchen of a military unit

explanation.surface: Setting up a smart kitchen almost entirely for vegetarians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'veggies' suggests vegetarians; here it means vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Legumes such as peas, beans and lentils are vegetables.

clue.text: Transforming aluminium into gold, mad guru

indicators.note: transforming changes one thing for another
into names what the replaced letters become

parts.note: mental is slang for mad
AL is the chemical symbol for aluminium
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A crazy spiritual teacher claims to turn base metal into gold, like an alchemist.
explanation.definitionFit: A guru is a trusted teacher or adviser, like a mentor.

clue.text: Burn marks inside hatch

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to hatch a scheme is to create it
M is short for marks, the former German currency

explanation.surface: Scorch marks found inside an escape hatch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hatch' looks like a noun, a door; it is the verb, to devise.
explanation.definitionFit: To cremate is to reduce a body to ashes by burning.

clue.text: Oddly, bechamel, not meat, is star of the show

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are rearranged
not means the following letters are left out

parts.note: ham is meat

explanation.surface: Remarkably, a bechamel sauce without meat is the highlight of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove HAM from BECHAMEL and rearrange the rest. 'Oddly' looks like a pick of odd letters; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeb, short for celebrity, is a famous person, the star.

clue.text: Make cuts in England, to the East being favourable

indicators.note: in an across entry, east is to the right, so this part follows

parts.note: rave, as in a rave review, means highly favourable

explanation.surface: Someone proposes making economic cuts in England and finds the eastern region keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make cuts in' sounds like budget cuts; it means carving lines into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Engraving is carving or incising a design into a hard surface.

clue.text: Half of US houses originally beige colour

indicators.note: housing something means holding it inside
half of means the first half of the word

parts.note: the US is America

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter

explanation.surface: Half the homes in America were originally painted beige.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a yellowish-orange colour, like the fossil resin.

clue.text: Potty is toilet promptly emptied

parts.note: a loo is a toilet

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: A child's potty is a toilet that needs emptying right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like a child's toilet; it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Potty and loopy are both informal British words for slightly crazy.

clue.text: Worthy bridge opponents — I'm invited into their play area

parts.note: in bridge, East and South are players on opposing sides, E and S

indicators.note: being invited into means going inside

parts.note: bridge is played at a card table
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A bridge player boasts of being invited to join a respected pair's game.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimable means deserving esteem, so worthy of respect.

clue.text: Friend more knowledgeable about energy drink

parts.note: bud is American slang for a friend

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: wiser means knowing more
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A smarter mate talks about an energy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Budweiser is a well-known brand of lager, so a drink.

clue.text: One favouring autocrat's sleeveless attire

indicators.note: sleeves are the outer parts, so removing them strips the first and last letters

parts.note: a tsarist supports the rule of a tsar, an autocrat; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A supporter of a dictator wears clothes without sleeves.
explanation.definitionFit: Saris are the draped garments worn by women in South Asia, so items of attire.
